title: The Mostowski collapse: representing well-founded relations by membership

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 30–31 (§6, Theorem 6.6, Definition 6.10, and Theorem 6.11; restricted here to set-sized carriers)

summary: A well-founded extensional relation on a set has a unique representation as membership on a transitive set.
abstract: An abstract relation can sometimes be represented exactly by membership between sets. If every nonempty group of points has a point with no predecessor in that group, and distinct points have different predecessor sets, each point has a unique set representing it. These sets preserve every link of the original relation and contain all their members within the representation. The hypotheses prevent membership loops and stop distinct points from merging, while a well-order gives an ordinal as its representation.
